data.outcome_summary: This OECD report chapter set describes how PISA 2000 (reading as the focus domain in 2000) can be linked to Canada’s longitudinal Youth in Transition Survey (YITS) to study pathways from age 15 to young adulthood. The Canadian cohort consists of 29 687 students who participated in PISA 2000 and were followed every two years through YITS, with additional parent and school information collected in the initial wave. The report explains that PISA provides benchmarked cognitive proficiency on a scaled metric (OECD mean 500, SD 100) and, for reading, proficiency levels with cut-points used for policy interpretation. It also documents that attrition in the longitudinal follow-up was addressed using special weights applied to analyses, though the excerpt does not provide the exact weight variable names or missing-data rules for covariates. Across chapters, the report emphasizes predictive associations between early PISA achievement and later educational attainment, persistence, course choice, and labour market outcomes, while cautioning that cross-sectional PISA alone cannot support causal claims.
